statement: The function returns a result r and r = numBottles + ((numBottles - 1) div (numExchange - 1)), where div denotes integer division (the floor of the real quotient). Equivalently, r is the maximum number of water bottles that can be drunk starting with numBottles full bottles and no empty bottles, when every exchange of numExchange empty bottles yields one full bottle.
preconditions: 1 <= numBottles <= 100 and 2 <= numExchange <= 100, interpreting both parameters as mathematical integers.

statement: The function returns a result r for every input satisfying the preconditions; it never fails due to overflow, panic, or out-of-bounds access.
preconditions: 1 <= numBottles <= 100 and 2 <= numExchange <= 100, interpreting both parameters as mathematical integers.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r >= numBottles.
preconditions: 1 <= numBottles <= 100 and 2 <= numExchange <= 100, interpreting both parameters as mathematical integers.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= 2*numBottles - 1.
preconditions: 1 <= numBottles <= 100 and 2 <= numExchange <= 100, interpreting both parameters as mathematical integers.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r >= numBottles + 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists a finite sequence of legal operations—starting with numBottles full bottles and zero empty bottles, where a drink turns one full bottle into one empty bottle and an exchange consumes exactly numExchange empty bottles to produce one full bottle—that drinks exactly r bottles.
preconditions: 1 <= numBottles <= 100 and 2 <= numExchange <= 100, interpreting both parameters as mathematical integers.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, every finite sequence of legal operations starting with numBottles full bottles and zero empty bottles drinks at most r bottles.
preconditions: 1 <= numBottles <= 100 and 2 <= numExchange <= 100, interpreting both parameters as mathematical integers.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, every legal process that performs exactly r drink operations and then stops ends with exactly ((numBottles - 1) mod (numExchange - 1)) + 1 empty bottles.
preconditions: 1 <= numBottles <= 100 and 2 <= numExchange <= 100, interpreting both parameters as mathematical integers.
